content.text: MOA: anti-inflam via multi actions on several types of leukocytes
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod -> take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill, PO, rectal

: cortisol, as well as other steroid hormones, binds to intracellular receptors – the steroid-receptor complex enters the nucleus and acts as a transcription factor to turn on certain genes, causing synthesis of specific proteins which are responsible for its physiological actions
Increases BG, increases protein catabolism from muscle/bone, antagonist of insulin
Inhibits number/activity of cells involved in inflammatory response
Inhibits histamine release from mast cells
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/water retention, potassium loss
•Replacement therapy: adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) and congenital adrenal hyperplasia (defects in enzymes for steroid hormone synthesis)
•Dexamethasone suppression test (DST): diagnosis of Cushing’s syndrome
•Treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases:  RA, ulcerative colitis, asthma, SLE, eye and skin inflammation
•Treatment of allergic reactions: drug, serum, and transfusion reactions
•Immunosuppression: prevention of graft rejection after transplantation
: increased appetite/weight gain, fluid retention, emotional instability, insomnia, indigestion, bitter taste, increased BP/BG

: osteoporosis, GI (ulceration, bleeding), psychiatric (mood, psychosis), cataracts, glaucoma, CV (HTN, edema, hypokalemia), diabetes, hyperlipidemia, Cushingoid syndrome, growth failure, impaired wound healing, adrenal suppression, immunosuppression
PO, SQ, IM, IV; folic acid supp → ↓AE
alcoholism/chronic liver dz; preg & breastfeeding; preexisting blood dyscrasias (marrow hypoplasia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia); hypersensitivity; immunodeficiency

: antimetabolite; interferes with DNA synthesis, repair, and cellular replication by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR); MOA in RA is unknown, but is thought to be similar to the antineoplastic action: folate antagonist that inhibits synthesis of purines
: usually first choice of DMARD therapy
: pregnancy/lactating, alcoholism, hepatic disease, immunodeficiency syndromes, preexisting blood dyscrasias
: GI (N/V/D, stomatitis) alopecia, elevated serum transaminases, skin (rash, pruritis, urticaria), CNS (fatigue, HA, malaise)
•less common – bone marrow suppression, immunosuppression, interstitial pneumonitis, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis
: derivative of 6-mercaptopurine and acts as an immunosuppressive antimetabolite
: approved for severe RA; restrict use to pts w/ severe, active & erosive disease not responsive to conventional management

roles.drugs: Localized: high-potency topical corticosteroid (eg, clobetasol 0.05% cream); used when possible to avoid or reduce systemic corticosteroids

roles.drugs: Generalized: prednisone 0.5 mg/kg orally once daily, tapered after several weeks to ≤ 0.1 mg/kg/day maintenance; remission usually in 2 to 10 months, sometimes years of treatment
